queries: WITH g AS (SELECT eventannotm, AVG(instownpct) AS avg_inst FROM sentimentandfundamentals GROUP BY eventannotm), b AS (SELECT AVG(avg_inst) AS baseline FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_inst) AS mean_of_above_averages, AVG(g.avg_inst - b.baseline) AS mean_excess_over_baseline FROM g CROSS JOIN b WHERE g.avg_inst > b.baseline

responses.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT eventannotm, AVG(instownpct) AS avg_inst FROM sentimentandfundamentals GROUP BY eventannotm), b AS (SELECT AVG(avg_inst) AS baseline FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_inst) AS mean_of_above_averages, AVG(g.avg_inst - b.baseline) AS mean_excess_over_baseline FROM g CROSS JOIN b WHERE g.avg_inst > b.baseline

assumptions.assumption: NULL eventannotm forms its own group (GROUP BY keeps NULLs as one group), and AVG ignores NULL instownpct.
A group whose instownpct values are all NULL has a NULL average. It is still a group, but AVG skips it when computing the baseline and it is never above the baseline, so it is effectively excluded.
If no group is above the baseline (for example, all groups are equal), the query returns one row with NULLs.

assumptions.assumption: NULL eventannotm forms its own group (GROUP BY keeps NULL as one group). A group whose instownpct values are all NULL has a NULL average and is excluded from the baseline and from the above-baseline set, since AVG ignores NULLs.
If no group is strictly above the baseline (e.g., all equal), the query returns a row with NULLs.

assumptions.assumption: A NULL eventannotm forms its own group (SQL GROUP BY does this natively). Groups whose instownpct is entirely NULL have a NULL average and are excluded from the baseline and from the above-baseline set.
The baseline is the unweighted mean of group averages, not the overall average of all rows.
